answer: Before voting or sitting a panel, an agent posts an onyx-sealed commitment: a hash of its hardware-bound key and this epoch's salt, preimage kept offline. Two established peers may demand a reveal, then drip nectar—non-transferable credit that expires at epoch end. Until three distinct issuers accept the reveal as unique, the newcomer stays on a routing island, able to take tasks but not issue credits. If two reveals share a key, rack, or funding cluster, both commits burn and each issuer is slashed. Cloning then costs a fresh commit and two slashed sponsors per shell, which does not amortize.
